description: A release manager notices that different teams are using slightly different pre-release checklists and wants to understand which differences are harmless local variation and which create real launch risk.

user_profile.persona: 33-year-old release coordinator overseeing several product teams
user_profile.context: Releases still happen, but the underlying process has clearly drifted over time
user_profile.communication_style: Process-oriented and comparative, wants meaningful differences surfaced

fact_sheet.fact: Anya Petrova is the Release Coordinator for the Platform division at StellarForge Inc., overseeing three product teams.
Ben Carter is the Development Lead for Team Phoenix, which is responsible for the 'Nova Platform'.
Chloe Davis is the QA Lead for Team Griffin, responsible for testing the 'Orion Suite'.
David Chen is the SRE Lead for Team Chimera, which manages the reliability of the 'Lyra App'.
Team Phoenix's pre-release checklist is a Confluence page located at https://stellarforge.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PHX/pages/18874369.
Team Griffin's pre-release checklist is a Google Sheet named 'Orion Pre-Flight v2.3' stored in a shared drive.
Team Chimera's pre-release checklist is a mandatory sub-task template within their Jira release ticket workflow, project key 'LYRA'.
The last modification to Team Phoenix's Confluence checklist was on October 5, 2023, by a former employee.
The 'Orion Pre-Flight v2.3' Google Sheet was last updated by Chloe Davis on January 15, 2024, to add a new security scan step.
Team Phoenix's checklist includes a mandatory item: 'Confirm all dependencies are updated to latest minor version in pom.xml'.
Team Griffin's checklist does not require updating minor dependency versions, only versions with a CVE score of 7.0 or higher.
Team Chimera's Jira checklist template includes a sub-task: 'Run `trivy` container scan and attach report with no CRITICAL vulnerabilities'.
Team Phoenix's checklist requires 'Manual QA sign-off from at least 2 testers,' while Team Griffin's requires sign-off from only the QA Lead.
Team Griffin's checklist includes a step: 'Verify rollback plan has been dry-run in staging environment within the last 7 days'.
Team Phoenix's checklist only requires that a rollback plan 'is documented and linked in the release ticket'.
The Lyra App checklist (Team Chimera) has a mandatory item to 'Notify #marketing-updates Slack channel 24 hours before release'.
Team Phoenix conducts their pre-release checklist review meeting every Tuesday at 3:00 PM PST via Google Meet.
Team Griffin does not hold a synchronous meeting; checklist items are checked off asynchronously in their Google Sheet.
Compliance with Team Chimera's Jira checklist is automatically enforced; the release ticket cannot be moved to 'Ready for Deploy' until all sub-tasks are closed.
Anya Petrova's analysis shows that Team Phoenix's checklist completion rate is 95%, while Team Griffin's is 82% over the last quarter.
On December 12, 2023, the Orion Suite release (v3.4.1) was rolled back due to a critical performance regression linked to an untested database migration script.
The post-mortem for incident INC-2023-451 recommended adding a mandatory dry-run of migration scripts to all checklists, but only Team Griffin has implemented it.
On November 20, 2023, the Nova Platform release (v5.8.0) caused a 15-minute outage because of a misconfigured feature flag, `ENABLE_NEW_DASHBOARD`.
Team Chimera, which uses the automated Jira checklist, has had zero release-related rollbacks in the past 6 months.
StellarForge Inc.'s official CI/CD tool is Jenkins, hosted at jenkins.stellarforge.internal.
Team Chimera uses a custom Jenkins pipeline that integrates with the Jira API to block promotion if their checklist sub-tasks are not complete.
Team Phoenix's release pipeline sends a notification to the #phoenix-releases Slack channel upon successful deployment to production.
The staging environment, staging.stellarforge.io, has its database refreshed from a sanitized production snapshot on the 1st of every month at 2:00 AM UTC.

Comparative launch-risk analysis for the three teams: Team Phoenix's requirement to update all dependencies to the latest minor version reduces version drift but, by itself, does not enforce a dedicated security scan step; Team Griffin's CVE-based dependency rule is narrower, but its process adds a recently introduced security-oriented control and a stricter rollback dry-run practice; Team Chimera's checklist requires an explicit `trivy` security scan with no CRITICAL vulnerabilities and is automatically enforced in Jira/Jenkins, making Chimera's release path the most explicitly security-gated of the three. The main launch risk difference is that Phoenix and Griffin rely more on manual checklist discipline, while Chimera has automated enforcement and a direct vulnerability gate.

user_needs.description: Where are the pre-release checklists for Team Phoenix, Team Griffin, and Team Chimera located, and what format are they in?
What was the cause of the December 12, 2023 Orion Suite release rollback?
Following the Orion Suite rollback, what was the post-mortem's recommendation and which team has implemented it?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning the cause of a past incident, the immediate next question is about the corrective actions recommended and their implementation status.

user_needs.description: How do Team Griffin's and Team Phoenix's requirements for rollback plans differ?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Learning that a rollback was caused by an untested script and that the fix was to add a dry-run (N3) naturally leads to investigating which other teams have this specific process gap in their rollback plan validation.

user_needs.description: What is Team Chimera's release rollback history for the past 6 months, and what is their checklist enforcement mechanism?
How does Team Chimera's Jenkins pipeline integrate with Jira to enforce their checklist?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After learning that Team Chimera has a perfect record due to automated enforcement (N5), the user will want to understand the specific technical implementation of that enforcement.

user_needs.description: How do the dependency update and security scan requirements differ between Team Phoenix, Team Griffin, and Team Chimera, and what do those differences imply for launch risk?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning that Team Chimera has a perfect release record with an automated checklist (N5), the user will want to compare specific items from their successful process (like security scanning) against the other teams' manual processes.

user_needs.description: What are the differences in QA sign-off requirements between Team Phoenix and Team Griffin?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After comparing one aspect of the checklists (dependencies), the user will likely continue comparing other key process steps like QA sign-off.

user_needs.description: What are the checklist completion rates for Team Phoenix and Team Griffin over the last quarter?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Once the user has identified the different checklists (N1), a quantitative measure of how well those checklists are actually being followed is a logical next step in assessing process health.

user_needs.description: What specific pre-release communication step is included in Team Chimera's checklist?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying Team Chimera as a model of success (N5), the user may be interested in other unique, positive process steps they've implemented, such as proactive stakeholder communication.
